result:
A race condition is a bug where the result depends on the unpredictable timing of concurrent processes touching the same state, so it works most of the time and occasionally corrupts or loses data.

For a shared log, always open with `>>`, never `>`. `>>` sets `O_APPEND`, so the kernel moves to the end of the file and writes in one atomic step, and writers cannot overwrite each other. Emit each entry as a single short `printf`, which is one `write()` call and will not interleave on a local filesystem:

```sh
printf '%s %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$msg" >>"$LOG"
```

If an entry is multi-line, built from several commands, or you read the file before writing to it, take a lock around the whole group:

```sh
(
  flock 9
  printf '%s start\n' "$(date -Is)" >&9
  some_command >&9 2>&1
  printf '%s end\n' "$(date -Is)" >&9
) 9>>"$LOG"
```

Every writer must use the same lock for it to work, and the lock is released when the subshell exits, even on a crash. Neither `O_APPEND` atomicity nor `flock` is reliable on NFS.
